title: Seventeen Sheets and One Crooked Line
subtitle: 艺术与设计 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 艺术与设计（文学艺术与体育·艺术与设计）
meta: 主题语境：艺术与设计（文学艺术与体育·艺术与设计）　|　核心词汇：design　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 design 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1950 the architect ① drew a design that no builder in the city would have quoted, and he said the drawing was the whole of the commission. The ② design, meaning the plan and not the pattern, ran seventeen sheets and stayed uncosted; a design, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unpriced.

Every ③ design in that office had the same crooked line across it, and the ④ design at the end, meaning the one they kept for the hall and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever revised twice. A design, his assistant said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to draw; the architect said the patience is the part that fills seventeen sheets.

The weaver meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the design was the whole of the cloth, meaning the pattern and not the plan. The ⑥ design, meaning the pattern and not any of that, is the only thing on a cloth that everybody praises and nobody counts; design, she said, is either something you draw or the only word that means both a plan and a pattern. She said the pattern is the part they remember.

By 1958 the ⑦ design had become a line in a contract, and the contract had become an argument about the crooked line. The ⑧ design of the whole thing, the architect wrote in June, was one office and seventeen sheets of drawing; design, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to draw. She said the drawing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ design I remember is the one at the end, which was built in 1973 and is still described as the strangest in the city. A ⑩ design, the assistant said in 1975, is the only thing that improves by being built; every design, she said, is a pattern that has agreed to look like a plan. She said the pattern was the honest half.

options: A. n. 设计；设计方案（指事务所里画出的那一份）

F. n. 设计（指合同里写到、被约定的那一份）
G. n. 图案；花样（指布面上织出的纹样）
H. n. 图案（抽象总称，指人人称赞却无人细数的那些）

answers.why: draw a design 意为“绘制一份设计”，1950 年建筑师绘制了一份全城没有一位建造商肯报价的设计。
design 意为“设计”，指那份方案本身而不是那个图案，它画了十七张纸而始终没有估价。
design 意为“设计”，指那间事务所里每一份设计，每一份上面都横着同一条歪线。
design 意为“设计”，指留给大厅用的那一份，是唯一有人修改过两次的。
design 意为“图案、花样”，指布面上织出的纹样，织工说这个图案就是那块布的全部。
design 意为“图案”，指人人称赞却无人细数的那些而不是那份方案，是布面上人人都称赞、却无人细数的东西。
design 意为“设计”，指合同里写到、被约定的那一份，到 1958 年这份设计成了合同里的一行。
design 意为“设计、图样”，建筑师六月写道，整件事的图样是一间事务所和十七张纸的绘制。
design 意为“设计”，我记得的是末尾那一份，1973 年建成，至今仍被说成全城最奇的一份。
design 为抽象总称，助手 1975 年说，一份设计是唯一会因为被建成而变得更好的东西。
